title: Indian Airlines Extend Saudi Suspensions, IndiGo Cancels Till November 14
excerpt: Air India and Air India Express keep Riyadh and Dammam suspended till November 7 and Jeddah till October 31, while IndiGo's Saudi cancellations now run to November 14 — with refunds and one free rebooking for bookings made on or before October 24.
body:
• Air India and Air India Express flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam remain suspended until November 7, 2026, and Jeddah services until October 31, in view of the security situation in Saudi Arabia.
  • IndiGo has cancelled flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah until November 14 — the longest current suspension among Indian carriers.
  • If your booking was issued on or before October 24, you are eligible for a full refund or one complimentary rebooking: travel by November 21 on Riyadh/Dammam routes and by November 14 on Jeddah routes.
  • Akasa Air's Riyadh suspension runs until November 30 and its Jeddah suspension until November 10, so check your own airline's date — there is no single Saudi deadline.

Indian airlines have extended their suspensions of Saudi Arabia flights on staggered schedules, with Air India and Air India Express holding Riyadh and Dammam services until November 7 and Jeddah until October 31, while IndiGo's cancellations across four Saudi cities now run until November 14, according to airline advisories collated by TravelObiz.

The suspensions, first imposed as the security situation around Saudi Arabia disrupted regional airspace, are being rolled forward carrier by carrier rather than lifted together. Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport is operating a limited schedule, and foreign carriers including Air France and Lufthansa have also pushed their Riyadh returns into mid-November and beyond.

What Each Airline Is Doing

Air India and Air India Express said flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam will remain suspended until November 7, 2026, while services to and from Jeddah will remain suspended until October 31, as reported by Time Out Riyadh. Guests holding confirmed bookings issued on or before October 24 may take flexible rebooking or a full refund.

The rebooking windows differ by route. Air India passengers on Riyadh and Dammam bookings with original travel dates up to November 7 can make one complimentary change to or from any operational Air India station in Saudi Arabia, for travel completed by November 21. Jeddah passengers with travel dates up to October 31 get the same one-time change, for travel by November 14. Air India Express passengers can rebook through the airline's operational stations in Saudi Arabia or Bahrain and India, on the same deadlines.

IndiGo's suspension is broader and longer: flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah remain cancelled until November 14, citing regional airspace restrictions. Akasa Air has extended its Riyadh suspension to November 30 and Jeddah to November 10. Etihad has cancelled Abu Dhabi services to Dammam, Riyadh and Jeddah through November 5.

What Passengers Should Do Now

The October 24 cutoff is the detail that matters most. If your ticket was issued on or before that date, the refund and free-rebooking offers apply; tickets bought later are governed by the fare rules in force when you booked. Air India passengers can call +91 11 69329333 or +91 11 69329999, and Air India Express passengers +91 124 6935600.

Do not assume a flight operates simply because its suspension date has passed — these are rolling suspensions that have already been extended once, and airlines are confirming resumptions route by route. Check your specific flight status before travelling to the airport, and confirm any onward hotel, Umrah or connecting arrangements against the new dates.

Why This Matters for the Diaspora

Saudi Arabia hosts one of the largest Indian expatriate communities in the world, and the Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam routes carry workers returning to jobs, families visiting relatives and Umrah pilgrims. A suspension that stretches into mid-November falls across a heavy travel period, and the staggered end dates mean a family split across two airlines may find one ticket restored weeks before the other.

What's Next

Watch for the next advisory cycle in the first week of November. If the security situation stabilises, Air India's Jeddah route is the first due back, on October 31, followed by Riyadh and Dammam on November 7. Any further extension would most likely be announced a few days before those dates, as the current ones were.
